rulingTitle: A bot push made before B’s review can still clear B’s finding if its commit was absent from B but later merged into C: the push is now in range even though it predates the finding.

action.reason: Hold. A push made before B’s review can clear B’s blocker if C later reaches that commit and B did not. Do not clear a carried finding unless there is reliable evidence that the matching push came after the review that raised it.

rationale: review-run.ts passes the ancestry-based inRange list as carriedFixPushes. review-convergence.ts checks reachability, not timing, and carriedOpen removes a finding on a matching key alone. The existing test injects an already-selected push; it does not test a pre-review push merged later.

rulingTitle: If the only matching artifact has a non-array `agreed`, the loader rejects it and returns `null`, so the review stays narrow; a newer artifact with missing `agreed` or unusable findings can also mask an older usable artifact.

action.reason: Hold. The carry reader must distinguish no matching artifact from matching artifacts that are all unusable. Try older usable matches before widening; keep the narrow range only when no matching artifact exists or a usable match was found.

rationale: The loader rejects non-array agreed before the carry reader can see that the artifact matched, so a lone malformed match becomes null and the range stays narrow. Missing agreed or wholly unusable findings can instead win by modification time and force an unnecessary full review despite an older usable match. Keep the existing fix-loader test that expects null for a lone malformed artifact; add carry-specific tests using the real loader for both cases.

rulingTitle: The new carry format drops the finding’s trigger, and the artifact fallback also strips it. For example, a blocker classified as `own-concurrency` is read back as `normal` and dropped under a policy that blocks only `own-concurrency`.

action.reason: Hold. Losing the trigger can silently release a blocker without a fix or ruling. Preserve and validate trigger and triggerEvidence through both the forge record and the artifact fallback.

rationale: The forge-record projection and parser omit both fields. The original artifact can contain them, but the fallback reader strips them. isBlockingFinding then treats the missing trigger as normal, so an own-concurrency blocker disappears under an own-concurrency-only policy. Test that policy through both round trips.

rulingTitle: A `--full` rerun of an already-indexed head can overwrite its valid carry record with an empty one even when it leaves files unread. Holding the index advance cannot protect the old record because the index already points to that head, so the next incremental review trusts the replacement.

action.reason: Hold. Preserve the existing carry record until a fully read, successfully posted review can replace it without dropping findings. Holding the index advance is not enough when the index already points to that head.

rationale: A full rerun does not load the previous carry, and postPrReview writes the replacement before it knows whether replies, the summary, and the coverage record landed. postCarriedRecord also writes budget-truncated payloads before returning failure. A later incremental review accepts the valid-looking empty or partial replacement. Test that unread files, failed posts, and budget overflow leave the prior carry intact without changing unread-file coverage reporting.

rulingTitle: The case-sensitive repository comparison can make `nax bot fix` report no review when two checkouts of the same GitHub repository spell the owner or repository name with different casing.

action.reason: Hold. A case-only GitHub slug mismatch can wrongly refuse a fix. It can also hide the earlier code review from readiness when a newer conversation-only artifact matches the current casing.

rationale: resolvePrRef preserves the checkout’s slug spelling, and samePr compares it literally. fixCheckout refuses if neither artifact matches; if only the conversation-only artifact matches, readiness falls back to it and can miss summary-only blockers from the code review. Compare GitHub slugs case-insensitively while retaining the forge, host, PR number, and exact-head checks and leaving GitLab matching unchanged.
